newsitem.title: USA: Greenway Partners considering bid for Outboard Marine.
newsitem.headline: Greenway Partners considering bid for Outboard Marine.

text.p: Greenway Partners LP and affiliates said Monday they are considering a bid for Outboard Marine Corp. that could top a $500 million proposal made last month by Detroit Diesel Corp.
The Greenway groups, which together hold about 9.9 percent of Outboard's common stock, made the disclosure in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Outboard Marine, based in Waukegan, Ill., is the largest U.S. maker of outboard engines and second-largest boat maker.

Greenway's bid would compete with one made last month by Detroit Diesel, a maker of truck engines and other equipment controlled by the Penske Group. Detroit Diesel offered to buy Outboard Marine for $500 million, or $16 a share.
Greenway, a New York-based investment group, could not immediately be reached for further comment.
A spokeswoman for Detroit Diesel, based in Detroit, said, "We have a tender offer that's outstanding and (Detroit Diesel) shares are pending registration. We, therefore, have no comment."

Analysts said Greenway acquired its stake in Outboard Marine earlier this year in the high teens to low 20s, as did speculators who had wagered that it would be acquired for more than the price offered last month by Detroit Diesel.
Shares in Outboard Marine rose 12.5 cents to $16.125; Detroit Diesel stock fell 12.5 cents to $25.31, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
